Judgment:
1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954
(Pfa Act), alleging that the accused persons have violated the provisions of the Pfa Act and Rules

2. As per the complaint, on 05.06.1999 at about 11:00 am, food officials consisting of Food Inspectors (herein after referred to as FI) Dharam Pal Singh lifted/purchased a sample of pasturised full cream milk from accused Shyam Singh, Driver of the vehicle No. HR-38-C-6617 belongs to M/s Bhagwati Transport Services (deployed by Mother Diary) parked at Link Road, Anand Vihar ISBT,
Delhi, where the said food articles was found stored for sale and accused Shyam Singh was found conducting the business of the said food article at the time of sampling.
The said sample was taken under the direction of LHA/SDM Sh C. Udai Kumar.
The sample consisted of approx 1000 ml.
Pasturised full cream milk was taken out from two sealed polypack of 500 ml each having label declaration as "Pasturised Full Cream Milk".
The DA vs Shyam Singh etc. sample of milk was taken out from two sealed polypackets.

Before taking the sample, the polypack duly shaken in all direction then cut the both polypacks from the corner then poured into dry and clean jug and properly homogenised with the help of dry and clean spoon.
Thereafter, FI divided the sample then and there into three counter-parts by putting them in three separate clean and dry glass bottles.
27 drops of formalin was added in each counterpart of the sample bottle.
Each bottle containing the sample were separately, fastened, marked and sealed according to PFA Act & Rules.
The vendor's signature were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample bottles.
Notice was given to the accused Shyam Singh and the price of the sample was also given to him.
Panchanama was prepared at the spot.
All the documents prepared by FI were signed by the accused as well as by the witness Sh A.K. Singh FI.
Before starting sample proceeding efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward.
3. One counterpart of the sample was sent to Public Analyst (herein after referred to as PA), Delhi in intact condition and two counterparts were deposited with LHA in intact conditions.
Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the sample to be adulterated being non-conforming to the standards prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules.

The report of the PA is as follows:-
"The sample does not conform to the standards because milk fat is less than the prescribed minimum limit of 6.0%"
4.

It is further the case of the complainant that accused Shyam Singh was the vendor-cum-driver of vehicle No. HR-38-C-6617 DA vs Shyam Singh etc. belonging to M/s Bhagwati Transport Services Da vs Shyam Singh Etc. on 2 April, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21634276/

The sample commodity had been processed and packed by M/s Gangol Sahakari Dugdh Utpadak Sangh Ltd., Partappur, Meerut (UP) as per the agreement with accused No. 2 M/s Mother diary and accused No. 5 P.P. Bhatnagar was found to be person incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the said concern, being its nominee.

sentences.text: The complaint was then filed in the court on 14.02.2000 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(a)(d) and (m) of PFA Act, as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act by the accused.
6. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 14.02.2000.
The accused thereafter exercised their option of analysing the counter part through CFL under section 13 (2) of the PFA Act.

Notice under section 251 Cr.P.C was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1) (a) PFA Act being violation of Rule A.11.01.11, Rule 65(2)
and Section 2(ia)(a)&(m) of PFA Act, to which accused pleaded not DA vs Shyam Singh etc. guilty and claimed trial.
7.
At the trial, the prosecution examined two witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 Sh. A.K. Singh and PW-2 Uday Kumar SDM/LHA.
PW-1 & PW-2 were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh Uday Kumar.

They narrated the steps undertaken by them, during the sample proceedings, including disclosing identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting of sample of two sealed polypack of 500 ml each of pasturized full cream milk, cutting the polypack from one corner and contents were poured into sample bottles, adding 40 drops of formalin in each bottle, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses.
They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex. PW-1/A, Notice Ex. PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C and statement of accused Brij Mohan Lamba owner of tanker Ex.PW1/D.

Thereafter one counterpart of sample along with Memo as per Form-VII were deposited to PA for analysis vide Ex.
PW-2/A and remaining two counter parts along with copies of Form VII were deposited with LHA vide LHA receipt Ex.PW2/B.
Thereafter the PA Report Ex.PW-2/C was received and on the direction of PW-2, FI D.P. Singh conducted the investigation.

On completion of investigation, FI D.P. Singh put the entire file before PW-2 and PW-2 forwarded the same to the then Director PFA and obtained the consent for prosecution Ex.PW2/D against the accused persons.

Thereafter, FI D.P. Singh sent letter Ex.PW2/F to L.K. Sharma Marketing Officer, Mother Diary Parparganj and letter Ex.PW2/G to accused No. 6 M/s Gangole Sahkari Dudh Utpadak DA vs Shyam Singh etc.

Thereafter, the matter was listed for defence evidence.
9. In their defence, the accused No. 5 P.P. Bhagnagar examined himself as DW-1.

Thereafter, vide order dated 19.10.2016 defence evidence was closed and the matter was fixed for final arguments.
10.
In a criminal case, the burden is only on the prosecution to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt by leading positive evidence.
This burden cannot be shifted to the accused and it has to be necessary discharged by the prosecution itself.
11.The present case alleges adulteration in the sample of "Pasturised Full Cream Milk" collected from the vehicle of the accused no. 1.
This sample of Milk has been analysed twice, firstly by the PA and secondly, by the CFL.
12. The prime argument of the Ld. Defence Counsel on the basis of which acquittal is sought at the threshold in this matter is thus, DA vs Shyam Singh etc.

'since there is variation of more than 0.3%
in the reports of PA and CFL, the samples were not representative'.

Pointing out the above said variation in the presence of colour total soluble solids, it is contended that the same would be sufficient to conclude that samples were not taken by the FI in proper manner and were not representative, for which benefit should be given to the accused.
The variation in the present case in respect of the fat content is also more then 0.03 percent.
The PA report shows fat as 5.5 whereas CFL shows it as 5.2%.

13. In this regard, the defence strongly relies upon the judgement titled as Kanshi Nath v. State [2005(2) FAC 219], informing that the said ruling has been followed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in State v. Ramesh Chand [2010(2)JCC 1250], Food Inspector v. Parvinder Malik [2014(2)
FAC 306], State v. Vinod Kumar Gupta [2010(2) JCC 957], State v. Virender Kohli [2014(2) FAC 223], State v. Kamal Aggarwal [2014(2) FAC 183], State v. Vidya Gupta [2014(1) FAC 291], State v.
Dinesh Goswami [2014(1) FAC 302], State v. Mahabir [2014(1) FAC 286], State v. Santosh Sharma [2014(1) FAC 296], Raja Ram Seth & Sons v. Delhi Administration [2012(2) FAC 523], State v. Sunil Dutt [2011(4) JCC 2377] and State v. Rama Rattan Malhotra [2012(2) FAC 398].

sentences.text: 14. As per section 13(3) of the PFA Act, the certificate issued by the Director of CFL shall supersede the report of the PA.
As per proviso to section 13(5) of the Act, such certificate shall be final and conclusive evidence for the facts stated therein.
Thus, as far as the findings of the CFL are concerned, the same are final and DA vs Shyam Singh etc. conclusive and no evidence can be given to disprove the same.

15. In Calcutta Municipal Corporation v. Pawan Kumar Saraf [AIR 1999 SC 738], it has been authoritatively laid down that the legal impact of a certificate of the Director of CFL is three fold: (a)
it annuls or replaces the report of the PA, (b) it gains finality regarding the quality and standard of the food article involved in the case and (c) it becomes irrefutable so far as the facts stated therein are concerned.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Subhash Chander v. State, Delhi Administration [1983(4) DRJ 100], it was observed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi that "It has repeatedly been held by the supreme court that the certificate of the Director supersedes the report of the public analyst and is to be treated as conclusive evidence of its contents.

entities.text: Subhash Chander v. State, Delhi Administration [1983(4) DRJ 100]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Director is a greater expert and therefore the statute says that his certificate shall be accepted by the court as conclusive evidence.
For all purposes the report of the public analyst is replaced by the certificate of the Director....
Superseded is a strong word.
It means obliterate, set aside, annul, replace, make void, inefficacious or useless, repeal.
The Director's certificate supersedes the report given by the public analyst.
Once superseded it does not survive for any purpose.
It will be anomalous to hold that for some purpose it survives and for other purposes it is superseded."
17. The scheme of Act would show that CFL has been, in a way, given the status of an appellate expert over the findings of PA.

In the landmark judgement titled as MCD v. Bishan Sarup [ILR DA vs Shyam Singh etc. 1970 (1) Delhi 518], the full bench of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi observed as under:
(a) The accused is entitled to get benefit of doubt if on account of delay or lapse on the part of prosecution to institute a prosecution, the Director CFL is unable to analyse the sample because of delay or of the sample undergoes a change for this reason.

entities.text: MCD v. Bishan Sarup [ILR DA vs Shyam Singh etc. 1970 (1) Delhi 518]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
( b) Once the Director has examined the sample and has delivered his certificate,
under proviso to sub-section (5) of section 13 of the Act, the certificate is final and conclusive evidence of the facts stated therein.
The presumption attaching to certificate again is only in regard to what is stated in it as to contents of the sample actually examined by the Director and nothing more.

Even after this certificate, it is open to the accused to show that in the facts of a given case and on the concrete objective grounds that he may prove on record the sample sent for analyses to the Director could not be taken to be a representative sample of the article of food from which it was taken.

( c) Despite the difference in reports, there was no effort to show that the sample sent to the Director,
CFL was not representative of the milk from which it was taken or that it had even otherwise undergone any chemical changes.
Proviso to section 13(5) would be attracted in full force as certificate of Director was final and conclusive evidence of the contents of the sample.

18. Therefore, although CFL report supersedes PA report but if the accused can show that the sample taken by the Food Inspector was not representative sample then he is entitled for a benefit of DA vs Shyam Singh etc. doubt.
In the present case, the PA report is also important because not only is there a variation but a contradiction between the PA report and the CFL report.
According to PA report, the the test for solids not fat was as per standard whereas as per CFL report it was below standard.
Therefore to this extent the reports are contrary to each other.
Therefore, such a contradiction on both the reports, gives a substantial clue in favour of the accused that the sample lifted was not a representative sample.

5 19.

On the basis of aforesaid discussions, the all accused are entitled for the benefit of doubt and are acquitted for the reason that the sample of "Pasturised Full Cream Milk" could not be said to be representative in character.
